Random-baseline sampling scheme: resolved as uniform-over-all-chunks (not uniform-over-docs-then-chunk), because the production retriever ranks and returns individual chunks, deduped to doc_id only after retrieval. Seed=42 fixed and reported, with a 5-additional-seed stability check.
notes: GUARDRAIL DEVIATION FROM WRITTEN PROCEDURE, DELIBERATE: the procedure as written says to run `python -m rag.bench` directly, but bench.py's run_combination() calls store.clear()+store.upsert() on the collection under test -- a DELETE+INSERT against the live production sure_rag DB, forbidden by this run's read-only-DB guardrail. Instead authored bench_readonly.py, which reproduces bench.py's exact query/scoring logic (identical hit_at_k/reciprocal_rank functions) against whatever is already indexed, performing zero writes; a local-vs-DB chunk-count cross-check confirmed the live index is current, so this is not a staleness concern. e5-small/heading reproduced the published MRR=0.856/hit@1=0.793 exactly. Honest caveat: the random baseline's MRR (0.418) is not near zero because the corpus has only 8 source documents, so even 5 random chunks span most of them by chance -- the hit@1 margin (real 0.793 vs random 0.207) is the least corpus-size-inflated, most defensible number.

Parseability-detection ambiguity: rather than use the written procedure's heuristic (reasoning==raw[:500]), reimplemented generate_decision()'s exact parse logic one level up over the same unmodified inference._decision_user_content()/inference._generate() primitives, yielding a definitive parse_ok boolean at no extra generation cost.
notes: CENTRAL FINDING, REPORTED HONESTLY EVEN THOUGH IT COMPLICATES THE HEADLINE NARRATIVE: the dominant observed pathway (50%, 4/8) is NOT 'the LLM reasons and the rule engine corrects a miss' -- it is malformed output defaulting safe, exactly the minimum-viable framing research_goals.json's own risk table pre-registered as legitimate ('malformed-output fail-safe is the dominant observed pathway, not severity-correction'). Only 1/8 scenarios (12%) shows the textbook under-call-then-escalate dynamic the unit tests establish is logically sound. Zero over-calls observed (n=8 too small to generalize this to 'rare in general'). A qualitative bonus finding grounds H2's scope boundary concretely: the model fabricates specific numeric sensor readings in free-text reasoning in 6/8 cases, sometimes reaching the categorically-correct status via an entirely invented causal story (T05, T08) -- this is structurally invisible to a status-only comparison and would pass through even the 'agrees' bucket undetected. Also fixed a namespace collision during implementation: llm-service/main.py and backend/main.py are both named 'main'; with both dirs on sys.path a plain `import main` silently resolved to the wrong one -- fixed by loading backend/main.py under an explicit distinct module name (sure_backend_main), not by editing either source file.

Format compliance and mean-steps do NOT reproduce exactly: this run measured AQUA-7B at 100% format / 2.0 mean steps vs. the published 60% / 3.6 mean steps, with no config difference found to explain it (adapter unset in both; loop.py unchanged) -- most likely mlx-lm/model-stack drift since the original table was produced; reported as a disclosed discrepancy rather than smoothed over.
